en: to rally; to muster; to gather allies

examples.ko: 그는 뜻이 맞는 사람들을 규합해서 새 모임을 만들었어요.
examples.en: He rallied like-minded people and formed a new group.
The opposition party is trying hard to gather its forces.

examples.ko: 동네 주민들을 규합해 반대 서명 운동을 시작했어요.
examples.en: They rallied the neighbors and started a petition against it.

examples.ko: 힘을 규합하면 더 큰 일을 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we pool our strength, we can do bigger things.

examples.ko: 팀장은 흩어진 의견을 규합하는 데 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took the team leader time to bring the scattered opinions together.
We need someone to round up our schoolmates.

explain: 흩어진 사람이나 세력을 한데 모아 한편으로 만드는 것이에요. '모으다'보다 힘이나 세력을 만든다는 목적이 분명하고 딱딱해서 정치나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그는 동지를 규합해서 새 단체를 세웠어요.
phrases.en: He rallied his comrades and founded a new organization.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻을 가진 사람들을 모을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for gathering people who share the same goal.

phrases.example: 우리 모두 힘을 모아서 이 일을 끝내 봐요.
phrases.en: Let's all join forces and finish this job.
phrases.nuance_ko: '규합하다'보다 쉽고 부드러워서 일상에서 두루 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and softer than 규합하다, so it works in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 흩어진 팀원들을 한데 모아서 회의를 열었어요.
phrases.en: I gathered the scattered team members together and held a meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흩어진 것을 한곳으로 모은다는 뜻에 집중할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the meaning of bringing scattered things to one place.

explain_en: Recruit like-minded people to form a group. It means gathering scattered people or forces into one side. Compared with '모으다', the aim of building power is clearer and the tone is stiffer, so it often appears in politics and news.

t90.ax: We need someone to round up our schoolmates.

examples.ko: 이 사진전은 한 가수의 사십 년 발자취를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This photo exhibition shows forty years of a singer's journey.
He is following in the footsteps of his seniors.

examples.ko: 이 책은 한 시인의 발자취를 소개해요.
examples.en: This book introduces the life path of a poet.
I went to my hometown to find traces of my grandfather.
I organized our company's history in photos.

examples.ko: 역사의 발자취는 박물관에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the traces of history in the museum.

explain: 실제 걸어간 자국에도 쓰지만, 사람이나 회사가 걸어온 역사와 업적을 말할 때 더 많이 써요. '발자취를 남기다', '발자취를 따라가다'처럼 써요. 발이 땅에 남긴 모양만 말할 때는 '발자국'이 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 그는 우리 역사에 큰 발자취를 남겼어요.
phrases.en: He left a big mark on our history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 업적이나 흔적을 남겼다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means leaving achievements or a mark behind.

phrases.en: I want to follow in my father's footsteps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 존경하는 사람이 걸어온 길을 따를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for following the path of someone you admire.

phrases.en: An exhibition looking back on the company's history is being held.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 역사를 되돌아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking back on past history.
phrases.en_equiv: to look back on the history

explain_en: It can mean actual footprints, but it is used more for the history and achievements of a person or company. Typical phrases are 발자취를 남기다 and 발자취를 따라가다. For only the mark a foot leaves on the ground, 발자국 is more natural.

en: to be energetic; to be solid; to be firm

examples.en: He is a friend who handles work firmly even though he's young.

examples.ko: 올찬 모습으로 새 출발을 한 그가 대견해요.
examples.en: I'm proud of him for making a fresh start with such a firm attitude.
This autumn's rice grains are plump and solid.

examples.ko: 올찼던 신입 사원이 벌써 팀장이 됐어요.
examples.en: The new employee who was so capable has already become a team leader.

examples.ko: 마음이 올차야 어려운 일도 버틸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You need a firm mind to endure hard things.
That child's voice is solid and confident.

explain: '야무지다'와 비슷하게 사람의 태도나 일 처리가 단단하고 믿음직할 때 칭찬으로 써요. 곡식 알이 꽉 차게 여문 것에도 써요.

phrases.example: 저 아이는 올찬 아이라서 뭐든 잘해요.
phrases.en: That child is capable, so she does everything well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 '올찬'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 올찬 before a noun.

phrases.en: She got even the hard task done in a solid, capable way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형 '올차게'로 일을 야무지게 하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb 올차게 describes doing a task in a solid, capable way.

phrases.en: My younger sibling works in a capable way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '올차다'와 비슷하고 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 올차다 and more common in daily speech.

explain_en: Like '야무지다', it is used as praise when a person's attitude or way of working is firm and reliable. It is also used for grain that has ripened plump and full.

examples.en: In his youth he was a famous orator.
My friend speaks powerfully, like an orator.
Lincoln is known as an outstanding orator.

examples.ko: 저는 웅변가가 되고 싶어서 연설 연습을 해요.
examples.en: I want to become an orator, so I practice giving speeches.
A great orator moves the hearts of the audience.

examples.ko: 웅변가의 연설에 광장 사람들이 귀를 기울였어요.
examples.en: The people in the square listened closely to the orator's speech.

explain: 사람들 앞에서 힘 있게 호소하며 연설하는 사람이에요. 말솜씨가 좋은 사람 전반은 '달변가'라고 해서, 웅변가는 연설하는 모습을 더 떠올리게 해요. 학교 '웅변 대회'와 같이 쓰이는 말이에요.

phrases.en: He spoke powerfully, just like an orator.
phrases.nuance_ko: '답다'를 붙여 웅변가에 걸맞은 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '답다' means behaving as an orator should.

phrases.en: I won a prize at the school speech contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들 앞에서 힘 있게 연설하는 실력을 겨루는 행사 이름으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of an event where people compete at giving powerful speeches.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 달변가라서 말을 정말 잘해요.
phrases.en: He's a smooth talker, so he speaks really well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연설뿐 아니라 말솜씨가 좋은 사람 전반을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to anyone with good speaking skills, not only speech-giving.

explain_en: This is a person who gives forceful, persuasive speeches in front of people. A person who is simply good with words is a '달변가', so 웅변가 evokes public speaking more strongly. It goes with words like '웅변 대회' (speech contest) at school.

examples.en: A reliable supporter came, and it gave me strength.
My friends came to the match as my cheering squad.

examples.ko: 팬들은 우리 팀의 가장 큰 응원군이에요.
examples.en: The fans are our team's biggest supporters.
The more supporters there are, the more energy I get.

examples.ko: 이번 일에는 응원군을 더 모아야 해요.
examples.en: For this job we need to gather more backup.
I had my family as supporters, so I didn't give up.

explain: 나를 응원해 주는 사람들이나, 힘들 때 도우러 와 주는 사람들을 가리켜요. '응원단'은 경기장에서 응원을 이끄는 단체이고, '응원군'은 힘이 되어 주는 사람이라는 느낌이 더 커요. '지원군'과 비슷하게 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: My family is my most reliable source of support.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿고 기댈 수 있는 응원 세력을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for supporters you can lean on.

phrases.en: I'll be my friend's supporter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 힘껏 돕겠다는 마음을 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you will wholeheartedly back someone.

phrases.en: I'm glad reinforcements showed up in a hard time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '응원군'과 비슷하게 쓰지만, 실제로 도와주러 오는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used similarly, but with a stronger sense of actually coming to help.

explain_en: It refers to people who cheer for you or come to help when things are hard. '응원단' is a group that leads cheering at a stadium, while '응원군' leans more toward people who give you strength. It is sometimes used much like '지원군'.

examples.ko: 우리 회사가 원하는 인간상은 정직하고 성실한 사람이에요.
examples.en: The type of person our company wants is honest and diligent.
I gave a presentation on the ideal type of person.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 새로운 인간상을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This movie shows a new image of a person.
Please write down what kind of person you respect.

examples.ko: 부모님이 바라는 인간상과 제가 되고 싶은 모습이 달라요.
examples.en: The kind of person my parents hope for differs from who I want to be.

examples.ko: 소설 속 인간상이 현실과 많이 닮았어요.
examples.en: The kinds of people in the novel resemble reality a lot.

explain: '이상적인 인간상', '바람직한 인간상'처럼 어떤 사람이 되어야 하는지 말할 때 써요. '인재상'은 회사나 학교가 원하는 사람이고, '인간상'은 더 넓게 사람의 모습을 말해요.

phrases.en: Schools should teach what a desirable person looks like.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육이나 도덕에서 좋다고 여기는 사람의 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the kind of person considered good in education or ethics.

phrases.en: This company's ideal employee is someone who takes on challenges.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 학교가 원하는 사람의 모습을 가리키는 더 좁은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A narrower word for the kind of person a company or school wants.

phrases.en: The novelist portrayed a new kind of person in the work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 작품 속에 사람의 모습을 표현한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means depicting a type of person in writing or a work.

explain_en: Ideal human model in general, e.g. in education or society (바라는 인간상) It appears in '이상적인 인간상' or '바람직한 인간상' when talking about what kind of person one should be. '인재상' is the talent a company or school wants, while '인간상' is broader.

examples.en: Our class united as one and took the championship.

examples.ko: 모두가 일치단결하면 어려운 일도 해낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If everyone stands united, even hard things can be done.

examples.ko: 위기 때마다 국민이 일치단결한 덕분에 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the people uniting every time there was a crisis, we got through it.
We ran to the end with a spirit of unity.
Our teacher always says that unity is important.
The students shouted a slogan calling for unity.

explain: 모두가 한마음으로 뭉친다는 뜻이라 구호, 연설, 스포츠 응원에서 잘 나와요. '일치단결해서 ~하다'처럼 하다를 붙여 쓰기도 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '다 같이 뭉치다', '힘을 합치다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 온 국민이 일치단결해서 위기를 이겨 냈어요.
phrases.en: The whole nation united and overcame the crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사에 '하다'를 붙여 동사로 쓴 형태예요. 구호나 연설에 잘 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding 하다, common in slogans and speeches.

phrases.example: 어려울 때일수록 다 같이 뭉쳐야 해요.
phrases.en: The harder things get, the more we have to stick together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 일치단결 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday way to say this instead of 일치단결.

phrases.example: 우리 힘을 합쳐서 끝까지 해 봐요.
phrases.en: Let's join forces and see it through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한마음이라는 느낌보다 같이 일한다는 느낌이 강한 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes working together more than being of one mind, and is easy to use in daily speech.

explain_en: It means everyone joins together with one mind, so it often appears in slogans, speeches and sports cheering. It can also take 하다, as in '일치단결해서 ~하다'. In everyday talk, '다 같이 뭉치다' and '힘을 합치다' sound more natural.

examples.ko: 그 단체는 젊은 사람들의 포섭에 힘을 쏟았어요.
examples.en: The group put its effort into winning over young people.

examples.ko: 포섭 대상이 된 사람은 처음에 눈치채지 못했어요.
examples.en: The person targeted for recruitment didn't notice at first.

examples.ko: 영화에서 스파이가 포섭 제안을 거절하는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene in the movie where a spy refuses an offer to be recruited.

examples.ko: 포섭이 성공하면 정보를 쉽게 얻을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the recruitment succeeds, they can get information easily.

examples.ko: 회사는 경쟁사 직원 포섭을 시도했다는 의혹을 받아요.
examples.en: The company is suspected of trying to win over a rival company's employees.

examples.ko: 돈을 앞세운 포섭으로 여러 사람이 넘어갔어요.
examples.en: Several people were won over by recruitment led by money.

explain: '설득'은 생각을 바꾸게 하는 일이고, '포섭'은 사람을 내 편으로 끌어들이는 일이라 더 정치적·조직적인 느낌이에요. 간첩이나 단체 이야기에서 나오곤 해요.

phrases.en: An intelligence agency's recruitment operation was in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 몰래 내 편으로 만들려는 계획적인 활동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A planned, secret effort to win people over.

phrases.en: He did not fall for the other side's attempt to win him over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끌어들이려는 시도에 설득되어 따르게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being persuaded by an attempt to draw one in.
phrases.en_equiv: to fall for an attempt to win one over

phrases.en: There was an attempt by a rival company to win people over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끌어들이려고 해 본 행동을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an attempt to draw someone to one's side.

explain_en: Drawing a person or group to your side, recruiting (신입 회원 포섭) '설득' is changing someone's mind, while '포섭' is drawing a person over to your side, so it feels more political or organizational. It often appears in stories about spies or groups.

examples.en: The working title of this documentary is 'Time of the Sea'.

examples.ko: 책 제목은 아직 가제라서 바뀔 수 있어요.
examples.en: The book title is still a working title, so it may change.
The director revealed the working title of the new film.

examples.ko: 가제로 쓰던 이름을 정식 제목으로 정했어요.
examples.en: They settled on the name used as a working title as the official title.
Shall we decide the working title of the article first?
As the drama's working title became known, expectations grew.

explain: 정식 제목이 정해지기 전에 임시로 붙이는 제목이에요. 방송, 출판, 영화에서 많이 쓰고, 보통 '(가제)'처럼 괄호 안에 적어요. 병원에서 쓰는 '가제'(거즈)는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I put a working title on it for now and submitted the proposal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식 제목이 없을 때 임시 제목을 정하는 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving a temporary title before the real one is set.

phrases.en: This drama was known by the working title 'Spring Day'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식 이름이 나오기 전에 사람들에게 알려진 이름을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the name people knew before the official one came out.
phrases.en_equiv: be known by a working title

phrases.en: I'll change the temporary title later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 쉬운 말이에요. 일상에서는 '가제'보다 이 말도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say the same thing, also common in everyday speech.

explain_en: Temporary title used before the final one is set (drama, film) It is a temporary title given before the official one is decided. It is widely used in broadcasting, publishing and film, and is usually written in parentheses like '(가제)'. The '가제' (gauze) used in hospitals is a different word that just sounds the same.

examples.ko: 큰 방향은 정했으니 이제 각론을 이야기해 봐요.
examples.en: We've decided the big direction, so let's talk about the details now.
We agree on the general idea, but opinions split on the specifics.

examples.ko: 각론으로 들어가면 세부 문제가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: When you get into the specifics, many detailed problems come up.

examples.ko: 회의 시간에는 각론보다 전체 계획을 먼저 확인했어요.
examples.en: In the meeting, we checked the overall plan before the specifics.

examples.ko: 이 책은 각론이 자세해서 공부하기 좋아요.
examples.en: This book goes into detail on the specific topics, so it is good for studying.

examples.ko: 각론 논의가 길어져서 회의가 두 시간이나 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The discussion of specifics dragged on, so the meeting took two hours.

explain: 반대말은 '총론'이에요. 뉴스나 토론에서 '총론 찬성, 각론 반대'처럼 큰 방향과 세부 내용을 나눌 때 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '세부 내용'이라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Now let me get into the details.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 이야기를 마치고 세부 내용으로 넘어갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving on to details after the big picture.

phrases.example: 세부 일정은 각론을 논의할 때 정해요.
phrases.en: We'll decide the detailed schedule when we discuss the specifics.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의에서 세부 사항을 이야기한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means discussing specifics in a meeting.

phrases.en: The overview is easy, but the details are hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '총론'과 짝을 지어 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with its opposite, 총론.

explain_en: The opposite is '총론' (general outline). In news and debates it is used to separate the big picture from the specifics, as in '총론 찬성, 각론 반대'. In daily speech, people often say '세부 내용' instead.

en: to devise; to come up with

examples.ko: 정부가 물가를 안정시킬 대책을 강구하고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is working out measures to stabilize prices.

examples.ko: 회사는 사고를 막을 방법을 강구해야 해요.
examples.en: The company has to work out ways to prevent accidents.
We worked out a plan to solve the problem.
I will work out a way to protect the citizens first.
We are in the middle of finding a way to cut costs.
Why don't you try working out another way?

explain: '대책을 강구하다', '방안을 강구하다'처럼 '대책, 방법, 방안'과 짝으로 써요. 회의, 뉴스, 보고서에서 주로 쓰고, 친구와 말할 때는 '방법을 찾다', '생각해 내다'가 자연스러워요. 사람이나 물건을 목적어로 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The city is working out flood countermeasures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 막을 대책을 찾을 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for finding measures against a problem.

phrases.en: The team came up with ways to cut costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의나 보고서에서 해결 방법을 찾는다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in meetings and reports for finding a solution.

phrases.en: We are working on a way to solve it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 방법을 찾는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you are still in the middle of finding a way.

explain_en: It pairs with words like 대책 (measures), 방법 (method) and 방안 (plan), as in 대책을 강구하다. It is mostly used in meetings, news and reports; with friends 방법을 찾다 or 생각해 내다 sounds more natural. A person or object cannot be its object.

examples.en: A swimming training session is held on the weekend.
My company told me to attend a security training session.
The training session starts at ten in the morning.
Since it's a free training session, many people are signing up.
I made a new friend at last month's training session.
We are preparing a training session for teachers.

explain: 수영, 요리, 안전 교육처럼 기술을 직접 배우는 짧은 모임에 써요. '강연회'는 한 사람이 이야기하는 모임이라서 '강습회'와는 달라요. 보통 '강습회가 열리다', '강습회에 참석하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: A cooking training session will be held next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 언제 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say when an event takes place.

phrases.en: The community center holds a photography training session.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임을 준비하는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the organizer.

phrases.en: I signed up to take part in the safety training session.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참석하다'보다 직접 배우고 활동에 참여한다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared to '참석하다', it has more of a feeling of actively taking part.
phrases.en_equiv: to take part in a session

explain_en: It is used for short gatherings where you learn a skill hands-on, such as swimming, cooking or safety training. '강연회' is an event where one person gives a talk, so it differs from '강습회'. People usually say '강습회가 열리다' (a session is held) or '강습회에 참석하다' (attend a session).

en: to give a public talk; to give a speech

examples.en: A famous writer gave a talk at our school.

examples.ko: 교수님이 내일 환경 문제에 대해 강연할 거예요.
examples.en: The professor will give a lecture on environmental issues tomorrow.
The speaker took questions at the end.

examples.ko: 그 의사는 전국을 다니면서 건강에 대해 강연해요.
examples.en: That doctor travels the country giving talks about health.
I gave a talk at the university and took photos with the students.

examples.ko: 무료로 강연해서 받은 박수가 가장 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: The applause I got from lecturing for free is what I remember most.

explain: 많은 사람 앞에서 하나의 주제로 길게 말할 때 써요. 수업은 '가르치다', 짧은 인사말이나 주장은 '연설하다', 일상 대화는 '이야기하다'라고 해요. 보통 '~에서 ~에 대해 강연하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The teacher gives a talk at the university.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강연하다'와 뜻이 같고, 목적어처럼 '강연을' 뒤에 '하다'를 붙여 말하는 자연스러운 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '강연하다', in the natural form where '하다' follows '강연을'.

phrases.en: Yesterday I listened to a famous writer's talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강연하는 사람이 아니라 듣는 사람이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by the listener, not by the person who gives the talk.

phrases.en: Right now, he is giving a talk in the big auditorium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강연이 지금 진행 중일 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A conjugated form used when the talk is happening right now.

explain_en: Use it for speaking at length on one topic in front of an audience. A class is '가르치다', a short address is '연설하다', and everyday chat is '이야기하다'. The usual pattern is '~에서 ~에 대해 강연하다'.

en: to reclaim; to cultivate; to pioneer

examples.en: He opened up a new market.
Immigrants cleared the wasteland and built a village.

examples.ko: 자기 길을 스스로 개척하는 것이 중요해요.
examples.en: It's important to carve out your own path.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 새 고객을 개척하느라 바빠요.
examples.en: The new employee is busy finding new customers.
The day will come when we explore and settle space.

examples.ko: 아무도 가지 않은 분야를 개척하고 나서 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: After pioneering a field nobody had entered, she became famous.

explain: 원래는 거친 땅을 일구어 쓸 수 있게 만든다는 뜻이고, 지금은 아무도 가지 않은 분야나 길을 새로 여는 일에 더 자주 써요. '새로 시작하다'보다 어렵고 도전적인 느낌이 있어요. '시장을 개척하다', '길을 개척하다', '고객을 개척하다'처럼 목적어를 붙여요.

phrases.en: He forged his own path in life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 만든 길이 아니라 직접 새 길을 연다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means opening a new path yourself instead of following one made by others.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 오래전에 개척되어 지금은 큰 도시가 되었어요.
phrases.en: This area was opened up long ago and has now become a big city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅이나 분야가 새로 열렸다는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, meaning land or a field was newly opened up.
phrases.en_equiv: to be developed; to be opened up

phrases.en: He is a pioneer of the space industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 분야를 처음 연 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who first opened up a new field.

explain_en: Opening new land or a new field. Originally it meant clearing rough land to make it usable; now it is used more often for opening a new field or path nobody has entered. It feels harder and more daring than a plain 새로 시작하다. Typical objects are 시장 (market), 길 (path) and 고객 (customers).

t90.ax: He opened up a new market.
